approachQuestion.prompt:
Fault-free spans. An array of signed readings is given. For each inclusive query [l,r], report whether every reading in it is nonnegative. Return q booleans.

Input: a=[0,-2,4,1], queries [[2,3],[0,2]]. Output: [true,false].

Constraints: 1 ≤ n,q ≤ 200000; 0 ≤ l ≤ r < n; -1000000 ≤ a[i] ≤ 1000000.

Which approach handles the complete task correctly and efficiently?

options.text: Build a leading-zero cumulative count of entries that are negative. A query is true exactly when its two boundary counts are equal.
options.feedback: The difference counts violations rather than summing values; zero violations is exactly the universal condition.

options.text: Build cumulative sums of the readings and accept a range when its total is nonnegative.
options.feedback: For [-1,2], the total is positive even though a negative reading occurs.

options.text: Check every entry of each query until a negative is found.
options.feedback: This gives correct results, but repeatedly traverses overlapping candidates. The selected summary reuses their shared work.

feedback.reason: Build a leading-zero cumulative count of entries that are negative. A query is true exactly when its two boundary counts are equal.
details: Build a leading-zero cumulative count of entries that are negative. A query is true exactly when its two boundary counts are equal.

A negative-count difference of zero proves no negative readings occur inside the interval. Summing readings instead would allow a positive value to cancel a fault. The summary tracks the predicate, not value magnitudes.

“Build a leading-zero cumulative count of entries that are negative. A query is true exactly when its two boundary counts are equal.”: The difference counts violations rather than summing values; zero violations is exactly the universal condition.
“Build cumulative sums of the readings and accept a range when its total is nonnegative.”: For [-1,2], the total is positive even though a negative reading occurs.
“Check every entry of each query until a negative is found.”: This gives correct results, but repeatedly traverses overlapping candidates. The selected summary reuses their shared work.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only the method in the reveal. Choose its tightest worst-case time and worst-case auxiliary-space pair. Use constant-time 64-bit arithmetic. Exclude read-only input and required output; include every described table. All loops are iterative, with no recursive stack or input copies.

options.text: O(n + q) time; O(n) auxiliary space
O(n + q) time; O(1) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Count negative indicators once, then compare two boundaries per query.
details: Prepare n indicator counts, then compare two counts for each query. Storage is n+1 counters.
Use constant-time 64-bit arithmetic. Exclude read-only input and required output; include every described table. All loops are iterative, with no recursive stack or input copies.

Preparation inspects n readings and writes n+1 cumulative indicator counts. Each of q requests reads and compares two counts, so total time is O(n+q). O(q) omits preparation when n dominates. O(nq) describes checking every reading in each requested interval, which this prepared method does not do.

The count table remains live with n+1 entries, giving O(n) auxiliary space. The O(1)-space option omits that table. The supplied readings/requests and returned Boolean answers are excluded; the table is newly allocated helper storage rather than part of the returned answers.
